approach: Integrate v = 40 − 10t to get the position x(t), then solve x(t) = 60 m and x(t) = −60 m for every non-negative time.

steps.text: Integrate the velocity to get the position, starting from x = 0 at t = 0.
The particle moves in the positive direction until v = 0 at t = 4 s, reaching a maximum x = 80 m, then moves back through the origin into negative x.
Solve x(t) = 60 m; the particle passes this point once going out and once coming back.
Solve x(t) = −60 m for the positive root, since the particle also reaches 60 m from the origin on the negative side.

common_mistakes.text: Stopping after finding t = 2 s and 6 s misses that the particle later reaches 60 m on the negative side too, at t = 4 + 2√7 s.
